subproblem.title: A.e. degree-one multiplicative homogeneity forces h(v) = c·v near 1
subproblem.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ 1 and let h : ℝ → ℝ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable on (1 − s, 1 + s). Assume that for every r ∈ ℝ with |r − 1| < s/4, h(ru) = r·h(u) for almost every u ∈ (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2). Then there is c ∈ ℝ with h(v) = c·v for almost every v ∈ (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (s : ℝ) (h : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → AEStronglyMeasurable h (volume.restrict (Ioo (1 - s) (1 + s))) → (∀ r : ℝ, |r - 1| < s / 4 → ∀ᵐ u, u ∈ Ioo (1 - s / 2) (1 + s / 2) → h (r * u) = r * h u) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᵐ v, v ∈ Ioo (1 - s / 8) (1 + s / 8) → h v = c * v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent-supplied proof (s₁ = s/4). Notation: I := (1 − s, 1 + s), I₁ := (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2), R := (1 − s/4, 1 + s/4), I₂ := (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8), I₃ := (1 − s/16, 1 + s/16); vol is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
0. (Arithmetic.) |r − 1| < s/4 iff r ∈ R, and then r > 1 − s/4 ≥ 3/4 > 0. Let u ∈ I₁ and r ∈ R; all four bounds are positive. So ru > (1 − s/4)(1 − s/2) = 1 − 3s/4 + s²/8 > 1 − s. Also ru < (1 + s/4)(1 + s/2) = 1 + 3s/4 + s²/8 ≤ 1 + 7s/8 < 1 + s, using s² ≤ s. Hence ru ∈ I. Moreover I₃ ⊆ I₂ ⊆ I₁ ⊆ I ⊆ (0, ∞).
1. (Borel version.) h is a.e.-strongly measurable on I, so there is a measurable h̃ : ℝ → ℝ with h = h̃ a.e. on I (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). The set {v ∈ I : h(v) ≠ h̃(v)} is contained in a measurable null set N.
2. (Transfer to h̃.) Fix r ∈ R. If u ∈ I₁ and h(ru) ≠ h̃(ru), then ru ∈ I by step 0, so ru ∈ N. The set {u : ru ∈ N} has measure |r⁻¹|·vol(N) = 0 (Real.volume_preimage_mul_left). Also h(u) = h̃(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁ ⊆ I. Combine these with the hypothesis h(ru) = r·h(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁: then h̃(ru) = r·h̃(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁.
3. (Quotient.) Let g(v) := h̃(v)/v, a measurable function. For r ∈ R and a.e. u ∈ I₁ (where u > 0 and r > 0), g(ru) = h̃(ru)/(ru) = r·h̃(u)/(ru) = h̃(u)/u = g(u).
4. (Tonelli.) The set E := {(u, r) ∈ ℝ² : g(ru) = g(u)} is measurable, since (u, r) ↦ ru is continuous and g is measurable. By step 3, for every r ∈ R (hence for vol|R-a.e. r), (u, r) ∈ E for vol|I₁-a.e. u. Now:
   - apply Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae to (vol|R).prod(vol|I₁) and the measurable set {(r, u) : (u, r) ∈ E}: a.e. pair lies in it;
   - transport through Prod.swap (Measure.prod_swap: the image of (vol|R).prod(vol|I₁) under swap is (vol|I₁).prod(vol|R));
   - apply Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae again to (vol|I₁).prod(vol|R) and E.
   Conclusion: for vol|I₁-a.e. u, g(ru) = g(u) for vol|R-a.e. r.
5. (Choice of u₀.) I₃ ⊆ I₁ has measure s/8 > 0. So by Measure.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae (for vol|I₁) there is u₀ ∈ I₃ with the property of step 4. Put c := g(u₀). Then A := {r ∈ R : g(r u₀) ≠ c} is null.
6. (Rescaling.) Note u₀ > 0. Suppose v ∈ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)) and g(v) ≠ c. Then r := v/u₀ = u₀⁻¹·v lies in R and g(r u₀) = g(v) ≠ c. So v lies in the preimage of A under v ↦ u₀⁻¹·v, which is null: its measure is u₀·vol(A) = 0 (Real.volume_preimage_mul_left). Hence g(v) = c for a.e. v ∈ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)).
7. (Containment.) 1 − s/16 < u₀ < 1 + s/16, and all factors are positive. So u₀(1 − s/4) < (1 + s/16)(1 − s/4) = 1 − 3s/16 − s²/64 < 1 − s/8. Also u₀(1 + s/4) > (1 − s/16)(1 + s/4) = 1 + 3s/16 − s²/64 > 1 + s/8, because s²/64 < s/16 for 0 < s ≤ 1. Hence I₂ ⊆ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)).
8. (Conclusion.) For a.e. v ∈ I₂, h(v) = h̃(v) (I₂ ⊆ I, step 1) and g(v) = c (steps 6–7). Since v > 0, h(v) = h̃(v) = v·g(v) = c·v. ∎
proof_key_steps: Arithmetic: |r−1| < s/4 implies r > 0 and r·(1−s/2, 1+s/2) ⊆ (1−s, 1+s).
Pass to a Borel version h̃ (null sets are preserved by u ↦ ru) and set g(v) := h̃(v)/v; for each r, g(ru) = g(u) for a.e. u.
Tonelli on (1−s/2, 1+s/2)×(1−s/4, 1+s/4) swaps the quantifiers: for a.e. u, g(ru) = g(u) for a.e. r.
Pick such u₀ in (1−s/16, 1+s/16); rescaling r ↦ ru₀ gives g = c := g(u₀) a.e. on (u₀(1−s/4), u₀(1+s/4)) ⊇ (1−s/8, 1+s/8).
Hence h(v) = h̃(v) = c·v a.e. on (1−s/8, 1+s/8).

audit.reason: Almost-everywhere strong measurability suffices through the measurable representative and null-set transfers under nonzero scaling. Tonelli correctly exchanges the exceptional-set quantifiers; the chosen u₀ and explicit interval bounds give precisely the s/8 window, including s = 1.
